target_customer: Food companies, restaurants and consumers of seafood in Asia
problem: Shrimp and crustacean supply has overfishing, pollution and farming harms; Shiok grows shrimp meat from cells.
business_model: Cultivated seafood producer, planned sales to restaurants and food partners

founders.name: Ling Ka Yi
education: Bachelor's and PhD, University of Wisconsin-Madison
founders.background_notes: Stem cell biologist with over a decade of research; A*STAR National Science Scholarship.

founders.name: Sandhya Sriram
founders.background_notes: Left on the Umami Bioworks merger per Green Queen.

competitors.name: BlueNalu
competitors.funding_then: 4.5M seed led by New Crop Capital

technical_complexity.rationale: Growing animal cells at food scale and cost was an unsolved research problem; needed cell lines, growth media and bioreactors.

defensibility.rationale: Cell lines and process know-how could be IP, but the field had several funded rivals and no commercial product by the batch.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it; Shiok bought Gaia Foods in August 2021 and then combined with Umami Bioworks in March 2024.

market_need_then: Cultivated meat attracted venture funding in 2018 and 2019; Shiok was positioned as the first Southeast Asian cell-based meat firm.

branding.name_origin: Takes its name from the Singlish and Malay word shiok meaning fantastic or delightful, per press and company profiles.

brand_strength.rationale: Local slang name with clear regional resonance and wide coverage, but the meaning is lost outside Singapore and the Shiok brand is to be retained only under Umami Bioworks.

pivots.to: Added cell-based red meat by acquiring Gaia Foods
pivots.why: Expand beyond seafood; terms not disclosed

outcome_analysis: Shiok raised a 4.6M seed in April 2019 and a 12.6M Series A in September 2020, and Green Queen said it had raised over 30M by March 2024. A full Series B was expected but no closing was found, and in March 2024 it combined with Umami Bioworks as CEO Sandhya Sriram left, citing shifts in the alternative protein sector. The exit looks like a consolidation of two cultivated seafood players rather than a financial win, but the price was not disclosed.
notes: A 3M bridge from Agronomics, VegInvest, Impact Venture and Mindshift came before the Series A per search summaries; date not confirmed so not recorded. Green Queen says over 30M raised while the sum of known rounds is about 20M; a Salestools page claims a 30M Series A at 100M valuation which conflicts and is ignored. Merger was a share-for-share deal per Agronomics. Company site returned 403. Competitor list holds only BlueNalu since other sources were not dated near the batch.
